script.text: Good morning! I'm Kelly, and this is your daily lesson for January 4. Today we're exploring two powerful ideas together.

Right now, light is racing toward your eyes at 186,000 miles per second.  By the time you process this sentence, light could have circled Earth seven times.  Today, we chase the fastest thing in the universe.

Light travels at 299,792,458 meters per second—and nothing with mass can ever reach that speed. As you approach light speed, time itself slows down. At exactly light speed, time would stop. Einstein showed us this in 1905. The sun you see right now is actually the sun from 8 minutes ago.  Look at the night sky—that star might not even exist anymore.
Today's wisdom: Here's today's wisdom: We are literally made of light.  Every atom in your body was forged in a star, created through nuclear fusion—a process that releases light.
Now let's take what we learned and put it into practice.
Today's growth challenge is Illumination - Finding Light.

Here's your activity: Make a list of three things that 'light you up'—activities, people, or places that energize you. Circle one you could spend more time with this week. This helps you identify sources of positivity and insight in your life.
And here's how today's lessons connect: What you learned about how light travels can be applied to illumination - finding light. Practice makes progress.
That's today's lesson. Learn something, grow a little. I'll see you tomorrow with something new. Stay curious!
